bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42490417 (c-blosc2): Heap-buffer-overflow READ 1 found by fuzz target decompress_frame_fuzzer [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42490417
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json issue_description / exact staged vulnerable source from gt-arvo_42490417-workspace:/src/c-blosc2 / patch.diff / sanitizer_trace.txt / reproduction_report.json / staged poc bytes
bug_description.normalized: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run reproduces the crash against the staged ARVO checkout `474ebf151be847186e6bc2c1381a8f7d4beff4dd`, whose line map matches `blosc_run_decompression_with_context:2147`. The exact 89-byte witness is admitted by `blosc2_frame_from_sframe()` because bytes 16-23 encode `frame_len = 89`, so `frame_len == len`, and the frame object aliases `frame->sdata` directly to the attacker buffer. `get_header_info()` then reparses the same bytes and materializes `header_len = 0` from bytes 11-14, `nbytes = 72057409955495950` from bytes 30-37, `cbytes = 0` from bytes 39-46, and `chunksize = 1459617792` from bytes 53-56; that yields `nchunks = 49367315`, preserves a huge `schunk->chunksize`, and makes the harness request chunk 0 with `nbytes = 1459617792`. Because `header_len + cbytes == 0`, `get_coffsets()` returns `frame->sdata` as if the entire frame were the compressed offsets chunk. `blosc_getitem()` then fails to recover an offset, emits the saved stderr `Error: problems retrieving a chunk offset`, and `get_coffset()` returns the sentinel `-4`. Vulnerable `frame_get_lazychunk()` never checks that negative return value on the in-memory path and computes `*chunk = frame->sdata + header_len + offset`, i.e. `frame->sdata - 4`. From that misbased pointer the next line reads `chunk_cbytes = 256` from original bytes 8-11, and `frame_decompress_chunk()` reads `nbytes_ = 65280` from original bytes 0-3; because `65280 <= 1459617792`, the `if (nbytes_ > (int32_t)nbytes)` rejection does not fire and `blosc2_decompress_ctx()` is called. `blosc_run_decompression_with_context()` then immediately dereferences `_src[BLOSC2_CHUNK_VERSION]` at line 2147 and ASan reports a 1-byte heap-buffer-overflow four bytes before the 89-byte input region. The staged `patch.diff` instead targets an older historical `blosc_d()` token-read check and does not match this live reproduced crash path.

source.description: First project-code statement on the crashing path that parses attacker-controlled frame metadata from the fuzz buffer.
source.value_from: The staged 89-byte `poc` stores `00 00 00 00 00 00 00 59` at bytes 16-23, so this statement materializes `frame_len = 89`, matching the full input size and keeping the buffer on the in-memory frame path.

root_cause.description: Root cause. After `get_coffset()` has already returned the error sentinel `-4`, the in-memory lazy-chunk path never checks `offset < 0` before using it as a byte offset. With the witness `header_len = 0`, this computes `*chunk = frame->sdata - 4`.
root_cause.note: The missing obligation on the witnessed path is an immediate rejection of negative `offset` values after `get_coffset()` fails, before either the file-backed or in-memory lazy-chunk branch uses that value as a real chunk offset.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer crash site. The decompressor trusts the invalid chunk base pointer and reads the version byte from `_src[0]`, which is four bytes before the 89-byte attacker buffer.
sink.note: Stage 01's saved ASan trace reports `READ of size 1` at this line with stack `blosc_run_decompression_with_context -> blosc2_decompress_ctx -> frame_decompress_chunk -> blosc2_schunk_decompress_chunk -> LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput`.

tainted_value_origin.description: This derives the compressed-offsets pointer from attacker-controlled frame metadata. For the witness `header_len = 0` and `cbytes = 0`, it points at the start of the whole attacker buffer instead of a real offsets chunk.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: Bytes 11-14 are `00 00 00 00` and bytes 39-46 are eight zero bytes, so this expression returns exactly `frame->sdata`.

parser_admitted.description: Once `get_header_info()` has accepted the staged frame header, this `copy=false` open-sframe path keeps the object as a frame-backed `schunk`, so later chunk requests go through `frame_get_lazychunk()` on the same attacker buffer with the header-derived `schunk->nchunks` and `schunk->chunksize` values intact.

evidence_limitations: The exact staged vulnerable source that reproduced the crash is the ARVO workspace checkout `474ebf151be847186e6bc2c1381a8f7d4beff4dd`, not metadata vulnerable commit `15f9cd0a160847d01e1aa18f00533f25cbe94e39`; every line number below is anchored to the staged checkout because it matches the saved ASan stack.

The staged `patch.diff` corresponds to an older `blosc_d()` token-read fix and does not patch the negative-offset path that the saved crash exercises, so Stage 02 cannot use that diff as direct fix evidence for this witness.

`run_flags.json` sets `runtime_disambiguation` to false, so Stage 02 did not instrument. The chain is closed from the staged source snapshot, saved ASan trace, reproduction_report.json, and direct inspection of the staged 89-byte `poc`.

coarse_trace.summary: The harness passes the attacker-controlled 89-byte buffer to `blosc2_schunk_open_sframe()`, and on the first loop iteration requests chunk 0 with `schunk->chunksize` as the decompression buffer-size argument.

The staged frame parser accepts `frame_len = 89`, aliases `frame->sdata` directly to the attacker bytes, and reparses malformed header fields `header_len = 0`, `nbytes = 72057409955495950`, `cbytes = 0`, and `chunksize = 1459617792`, producing positive `schunk->nchunks` and a huge `schunk->chunksize`.

Because `header_len + cbytes == 0`, the whole frame is misused as the compressed-offsets chunk; `blosc_getitem()` fails, `get_coffset()` returns `-4`, and `frame_get_lazychunk()` still computes `*chunk = frame->sdata - 4`.

From `frame->sdata - 4`, the lazy-chunk path reads `chunk_cbytes = 256` and `nbytes_ = 65280`; because the destination-size argument is the header-derived `1459617792`, `frame_decompress_chunk()` admits the decompressor call and the first version-byte read crashes four bytes before the 89-byte input region.

fine_trace.note: Source. The in-memory frame parser reads the serialized frame length directly from attacker bytes 16-23. In the staged witness those bytes decode to `frame_len = 89`.
The size sanity check is the first admission gate. Because the fuzz input length is also 89, the function does not return `NULL` and continues materializing the frame.
Because `copy` is false, the frame keeps a direct alias to the attacker buffer. Every later metadata read on this path dereferences `frame->sdata` rather than a validated copy.
Reparsing attacker bytes 11-14 yields `header_len = 0`. This is one half of the later `frame->sdata + header_len + cbytes` computation that picks the bogus offsets-chunk pointer.
Reparsing attacker bytes 30-37 (`00 ff ff d5 23 d5 00 0e`) yields `nbytes = 72057409955495950`. Together with step 7, that keeps the computed chunk count positive instead of zero.
Reparsing attacker bytes 39-46 yields `cbytes = 0`. Together with step 4, that makes the offsets-chunk pointer calculation collapse to the start of the frame buffer.

Reparsing attacker bytes 53-56 (`57 00 00 00`) yields `chunksize = 1459617792`. This attacker-controlled size is later exposed as `schunk->chunksize` and becomes the `nbytes` argument passed into `frame_decompress_chunk()`.

Because step 5 `nbytes` and step 7 `chunksize` are both positive, this branch computes `nchunks = 49367315` instead of zero. On the open-sframe path those results are returned into `schunk`, so chunk 0 remains reachable and `schunk->chunksize` keeps the attacker-controlled value from step 7.

fine_trace.code: dsize = blosc2_schunk_decompress_chunk(schunk, nchunk, uncompressed_data + i, schunk->chunksize);
fine_trace.note: The first loop iteration uses `nchunk = 0`, and because step 8 made `schunk->nchunks` positive, this call executes. Its fourth argument is `schunk->chunksize`, so `frame_decompress_chunk()` receives `nbytes = 1459617792` from step 7.
With step 4 `header_len = 0` and step 6 `cbytes = 0`, the in-memory path returns `frame->sdata`. The whole attacker buffer is now reinterpreted as the compressed offsets chunk.

Attempting to extract offset 0 from that bogus offsets chunk fails. The helper emits the exact saved stderr text `Error: problems retrieving a chunk offset` and returns the sentinel `-4` instead of a real chunk offset.

Root cause. The in-memory lazy-chunk path never rejects the negative `offset` error sentinel from step 11. With step 4 `header_len = 0`, this computes `*chunk = frame->sdata - 4`, i.e. a chunk base pointer four bytes before the attacker buffer.

Because `BLOSC2_CHUNK_CBYTES` is offset `0x0c`, this read lands on original bytes 8-11 after step 12 moved `*chunk` four bytes before the buffer. Those bytes `00 01 00 00` produce `lazychunk_cbytes = 256`, so `frame_decompress_chunk()` stays past its `chunk_cbytes < sizeof(int32_t)` short-input rejection and carries `srcsize = 256` into decompression.
With `src = frame->sdata - 4`, `src + BLOSC2_CHUNK_NBYTES` lands on original bytes 0-3. `sw32_()` therefore reads `00 ff 00 00` as `nbytes_ = 65280`.

The destination-size guard is bypassed because step 14's `65280` is smaller than step 9's `nbytes = 1459617792`. The `Not enough space for decompressing in dest` rejection does not fire, so execution proceeds to `blosc2_decompress_ctx()`.

The accepted invalid `src` and positive `srcsize = 256` reach `blosc_run_decompression_with_context()`. Since `srcsize <= 0` is false, this version-byte load reads exactly four bytes to the left of the 89-byte region reported by ASan. Stage 01's saved ASan trace reports `READ of size 1` at this line with stack `blosc_run_decompression_with_context -> blosc2_decompress_ctx -> frame_decompress_chunk -> blosc2_schunk_decompress_chunk -> LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput`.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: Stage 02 did not execute the fixed image, and the staged `patch.diff` does not touch the negative-offset path exercised by the saved crash, so it cannot be used as direct resolution proof for this witness.

poc.trigger: Pass the exact staged 89-byte `poc` to `decompress_frame_fuzzer`; the buffer satisfies `frame_len == len`, sets `header_len = 0` and `cbytes = 0`, encodes huge positive `FRAME_NBYTES` and `FRAME_CHUNKSIZE` fields, makes `get_coffsets()` treat the start of the frame as the compressed-offsets chunk, and after the unchecked `-4` offset causes `frame_decompress_chunk()` to admit a decompressor call from `frame->sdata - 4`.

format.name: serialized blosc2 in-memory frame
format.contract: Exactly the staged 89-byte buffer in `poc` (sha256 `4d70888458c1a928c4f0b17602f35dfdc13f72e7901a33158c46deae11265d9d`). Its verified trigger semantics are limited to the field values this witness sets: bytes 16-23 encode `frame_len = 89`, bytes 11-14 encode `header_len = 0`, bytes 30-37 encode `FRAME_NBYTES = 72057409955495950`, bytes 39-46 encode `cbytes = 0`, bytes 53-56 encode `FRAME_CHUNKSIZE = 1459617792`, and because the unchecked negative-offset path later reinterprets `frame->sdata - 4` as a chunk header, original bytes 8-11 are consumed as `chunk_cbytes = 256` while original bytes 0-3 are consumed as `nbytes_ = 65280`. Those exact witness facts make `get_coffsets()` return `frame->sdata`, make `get_coffset()` return `-4`, keep chunk 0 reachable, and make `frame_decompress_chunk()` bypass the `nbytes_ > nbytes` rejection before `blosc_run_decompression_with_context()` reads the version byte four bytes before the attacker buffer.
